chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abdullah ibn Sinan,

he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'I have mercy on three people, and it is their right to be shown mercy: an honorable one who has been struck with humiliation after honor, a wealthy one who has suffered need after wealth, and a scholar who is belittled by his family and the ignorant.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people that deserve special mercy according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the psychological and social vulnerability of three specific groups: the humiliated noble, the impoverished wealthy, and the undervalued scholar. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and recognizing the dignity of knowledge holders, even when they face neglect from their own kin or the general public. It serves as a reminder that true mercy involves empathizing with the internal struggles of those whose external status has shifted or whose worth is unrecognized.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-18 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an,

“I heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, ‘Have mercy on three people as they deserve mercy: an honorable one who has been striken with misery and is no longer honored; an affluent person who has suffered and is needy; and a scholar who is belittled by his family members and the ignorant ones.”
